title: Proofs run without a network seal, and standing seal records stay as written
intention: The tester stops cutting a network namespace around proofs: every run, seal, reseal and hollow goes at isolation none under the always-on instance seal, a standing 'sealed' record is left as written until its proof next runs for its own reasons, and that run lands with the retirement as its stated reason.
why: Akien via peer akiendelllinux_cc_0 as F39, 2026-10-08, verbatim: "it sounds to me like we don't need it at all... this is deeper than i designed. what i said was everything needed to be able to be worked on live. self testing, self checking... as long as things are working, we don't need to retest 400 proofs for something i never thought we needed." Measured 2026-10-08: the namespace's only recorded why (isolation.py:15-20, the 2026-07-13 incident) is the single inference slot, which moves to its owner in child d0672a46aa7e; meanwhile the seal costs every hollow run inside the verdict sandbox an exit 2 (c54d744aa9ac, worked around on 3d31d968a1a0 and 46ece5fd9f69). Folds the trouble at /home/akien/.cairn/logs/tester/0/20261008.190915.381284.TesterDevice.raise_trouble.json (F38), superseded by this ruling.
traces_to: RULE 1 (the tester stops enforcing a rule about inference_domain's resource); Law 4 (the slot rule moves to physics at its owner, d0672a46aa7e, binding every caller rather than proofs only); Law 9 + Akien's ruling (no mass re-run — a standing seal is not made red by a retirement); CP4 (the seal's cost serves no current consumer).
how: cairn/devices/tester: (1) isolation.py — NetnsIsolation is removed; get_isolation('netns'|'seal') raises ValueError naming the retirement (constant NETWORK_SEAL_RETIRED, which names this ticket and the ruling); the module docstring says the network seal is retired and why, and the instance seal is untouched. (2) cli.py — isolation_for returns 'none' for every run; --netns stays defined but refuses with exit 2 naming the retirement before any proof runs; the OVERRIDE print and the isolation_for_seal import go. (3) reseal.py:437 — iso = isolation or 'none'. (4) hollow.py — seal_isolation returns 'none'. (5) device.py:788 and reseal.py:501/558 pass unsealing_because=NETWORK_SEAL_RETIRED to persist_validation, which the store's own guard (validation_store.py:746-758) writes into evidence only when a measured seal meets an open reading — so a standing sealed record changes only when its own proof next lands, and says why. (6) The charter's 'owns the network' text is restated through the artifact door. validation_store is not changed (isolation_for_seal stays the store's vocabulary; the tester stops calling it). Proof changes are question open-41bc11343280. (7) cli.py — the `except (SealDowngradeRefused, SealConversionRefused)` lane (:579) is deleted with its imports if unused, and 299d4f72ae40's clause 4 is retired with it (open-914da176b1ed, Akien: "both look good to me"). (8) In the same act as the build: 481221f45884, 67af8b743a63 and 054bcbe02f12 cross PROVED -> SUPERSEDED, superseded_by d80360545e91 (open-0d44f8905e2e), and their proofs test_a_first_seal_is_taken_under_the_seal.py, test_an_unbuildable_network_seal_refuses_the_run.py, test_the_hollow_measures_at_the_seals_depth.py and probe probes/a_first_seal_is_taken_under_the_seal.py go through bin/cmd/trash with their seal records.
falsifier: Falsifier: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_network_seal_is_retired.py under PROVES {'d80360545e91': {'1','2','3','4'}}: (1) `cairn test --seal` over a fixture proof whose standing record reads sealed runs at isolation none (no --unshare-net in the sandbox argv) and lands green with evidence.unsealing_because naming the retirement, no SealDowngradeRefused, and a sibling fixture validation's bytes unchanged; (2) the reseal door over the same fixture lands green the same way; (3) hollow.seal_isolation reads 'none' for a sealed proof, and a hollow started inside an instance sandbox measures instead of refusing with SealUnavailable; (4) `cairn test --netns` exits 2 naming the retirement and runs nothing, and get_isolation('netns') raises naming it. (5) neither `cairn test` nor `cairn test --seal`, over fixture proofs standing at every seal verdict (sealed, open, breached, indeterminate) and one with no record, reports a refused seal or exits non-zero (open-914da176b1ed, answer A: the refused-seal lane in cli.py is deleted as dead, and this clause measures the premise on the build itself). Every instance-seal tooth (test_instance_seal.py, test_a_seal_inside_a_seal_inherits.py teeth 2-3) stays green. Hollow: reverting cli.py/device.py reds 1, 4 and 5, reseal.py reds 2, hollow.py reds 3, isolation.py reds 4. Horizon: the next PROVED crossing whose hollow criterion is `bin/cairn test --hollow <id>` runs it inside the verdict sandbox with exit 0 (c54d744aa9ac's exit 2 gone). Wrong intent if: a proof's correctness is found to depend on the network being absent, or any standing validation other than the one being run is rewritten by a run.
watchme: none, because the corpus reading is the existing probe /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn/devices/tester/probes/seal_measurements_are_not_dropped.py, which this ticket re-points (question open-41bc11343280 (e)) to count a record carrying the retirement as the standing reason rather than an escape

decisions.text: Build order, one file at a time, all in cairn/devices/tester/: isolation.py, then device.py, then cli.py, then reseal.py, then hollow.py, then the charter through the artifact door, then the retirements (trash the three proofs, the probe and three seal records; cross the three tickets SUPERSEDED). Proofs are NOT edited by the build: every proof change was made and committed before BUILDME (cairn 617adb9f, approved at open-41bc11343280, open-914da176b1ed, open-0d44f8905e2e). cairn/tools/validation_store is NOT edited (RULE 1).

isolation.py: add a module-level constant directly after the module docstring and imports: NETWORK_SEAL_RETIRED = "the network seal is retired by ticket d80360545e91 (Akien, open-41bc11343280): proofs run at isolation 'none'; the instance seal is untouched". Delete the whole class NetnsIsolation (isolation.py:723 through the end of its wrap method). Rewrite get_isolation as: if name in ("netns", "seal"): raise ValueError(NETWORK_SEAL_RETIRED); if name in ("none", ""): return NoIsolation(); raise ValueError(f"unknown isolation {name!r} — expected 'none'"). Leave every other function (inside_a_seal, SEAL_MARKER, bwrap_available, the seal verdict constants, the instance seal) unchanged.

decisions.text: isolation.py docstring: insert this paragraph immediately after the first line (the title line) and its blank line, leaving the rest of the docstring as history: 'THE NETWORK SEAL IS RETIRED (ticket d80360545e91, Akien at open-41bc11343280). Proofs run at isolation none; asking for netns or seal raises ValueError(NETWORK_SEAL_RETIRED). The instance seal below is untouched and still binds every run. Run from ~/dev/src/cairn, one command: bin/cmd/trash cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_first_seal_is_taken_under_the_seal.py cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_an_unbuildable_network_seal_refuses_the_run.py cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_hollow_measures_at_the_seals_depth.py cairn/devices/tester/probes/a_first_seal_is_taken_under_the_seal.py. Then git add -A on those four paths so the deletions are staged.

decisions.text: The reseal command is bin/cairn test --seal <proof>, one proof per command, run from ~/dev/src/cairn, for every file matching cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_*.py other than test_the_network_seal_is_retired.py (sealed first, by itself). A proof whose seal already reads green at the current source is still resealed, since the build changed the code it measures. Then run bin/cairn test cairn/devices/tester/proofs/ once (no --seal) and require the summary line to read 0 red.

Before trashing, run ls -l on the three seal record paths named in that line; all three were measured present on 2026-10-08. If ls reports any of them missing, do not trash the others or continue the build: stop and report the missing path to the peer session, since a seal record that moved is a fact the build cannot settle.
